title: FFA PRESIDENTS HONORED
full_story:
Two of the ten students recently named Illinois FFA Top 10 Chapter Presidents are from South Central Illinois.  They are Haven Cash of the North Clay FFA and Maliah Reichmann of the Nashville FFA.

Illinois Farm Bureau Youth and Collegiate Program Coordinator Lori Jackson says the outstanding students represent the future of agriculture and leadership in Illinois.  She adds their commitment, innovation and service to their chapters and communities embody the value of FFA, and they are proud to celebrate their accomplishments.

The FFA Chapter President award is sponsored by the Illinois Farm Bureau State Young Leader Committee.  Of the 44 applicants, the Top 10 and gold award winners will be recognized at the Illinois FFA State Convention in June.

Cash is also one of 10 candidates eligible for election to one of six Illinois FFA Major State Officer positions; president, vice president, reporter, secretary, treasurer or sentinel; at the 98th annual Illinois FFA State Convention in Springfield starting on June 11th.

Candidates were selected by a committee of agriculture industry representatives, media and collegiate leaders, past state FFA officers and current FFA members.  The elected state officer team will serve as student leaders representing nearly 400 FFA chapters statewide, with a focus on promoting agricultural education, personal growth and leadership.  Throughout the year, the team will travel to schools, facilitate workshops, meet with agricultural industry stakeholders and conduct conferences to inspire and engage FFA members.

title: NATIONAL DAY OF PRAYER
full_story:
Churches within the Clay City School District will be leading in prayer and music on the 75th Annual National Day of Prayer, tonight at 7:00 pm.  This year’s annual event will be hosted by the Clay City Community Southern Baptist Church (Route 50 – West of Casey’s).

The National Day of Prayer is a vital part of America’s heritage and is as relevant and critical today as it was at the first call by our Continental Congress in 1775.  Established in public law by a joint resolution of Congress, signed by President Truman in 1952, then amended to designate the day under the 100th Congress and President Reagan in 1988, it states that: “The President shall issue each year a proclamation designating the first Thursday in May as a National Day of Prayer on which the people of the United States may turn to God in prayer and meditation at churches, in groups and as individuals.”

Please join Clay City Church’s and exercise one of our most precious freedoms.  For additional information, please contact Clay City Area National Day of Prayer Coordinator, Pat Burt at 618-676-1783.

The Clay County Ministerial Alliance is having a National Day Of Prayer event tonight, at 6 pm at the Flora City Hall Flagpole.  If it’s raining it will be in the conference room at the library.  Everyone is invited to come and offer a prayer.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills were mailed out on Monday, April 20th.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you do not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: AGRICHEMICAL RECYCLING
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture encourages farmers and agrichemical facilities to take part in a free agrichemical container recycling program.  Beginning in the middle of July and continuing into August, sites throughout the state will collect containers that are recycled to make shipping pallets.

“Each year, this program gives farmers and agrichemical facilities an easy way to responsibly dispose of empty pesticide containers,” said IDOA Director Jerry Costello II.  “Instead of ending up in the trash, these containers can be brought to a nearby collection site and handled the right way.”

Metal and household pesticide containers are not eligible for the recycling program.  Collection sites will accept only high-density polyethylene, #2 plastic agrichemical containers that are clean and dry.  Participants are responsible for rinsing them and removing all caps, valves, metal, labels, booklets and foil seals.  Participants are also responsible for cutting off the top and bottom of plastic drums and cutting the side of the drum from top to bottom.

Mini-Bulk and Intermediate Bulk containers can be recycled via the Department’s container recycling program by making the following container preparations: Mini Bulk (cage) containers are required to be cut into separate top, bottom and sides, fittings discarded with no metal, and no wood.  Intermediate Bulk Containers are to be cut into one-foot square pieces, and fittings discarded.  G. Phillips and Sons, LLC is offering services to pick up Mini-Bulk and Intermediate Bulk containers throughout the year.  Call 678-232-6047 to learn more about their Mini-Bulk and Intermediate Bulk container collection service.

The program is a cooperative venture between the Illinois Department of Agriculture, Agriculture Container Recycling Council, GROWMARK, Inc., Illinois Fertilizer and Chemical Association, G. Phillips and Sons, LLC, Illinois Farm Bureau, and University of Illinois Extension.

The collection sites and dates in our area for the 2026 Pesticide Container Recycling Program are as follows:

In Wayne County collection is on July 20th at Wabash Valley Service Company in Ellery, for more information call Ken Ochs at 618-516-1697.  In Effingham County collection is on July 21st at Effingham Equity in Montrose, for more information call 217-254-1435. And in Fayette County collection is on July 21st at Nutrien Ag Solutions in Vandalia, for more information call Dylan Reeter at 618-780-8663.  All sites will be open from 9 am to 11 am and from 1 pm to 3 pm.

To obtain a free brochure about the program, call the Illinois Department of Agriculture toll free at 1-800-641-3934.

title: EASTERN ILLINOIS FOODBANK COMING
full_story:
The Eastern Illinois Foodbank will be in Clay County on Monday, to distribute food to area families facing food insecurity.  Those attending are asked to bring boxes or bags to transport their food in.

The Foodmobile will be at the Louisville Baseball Field where they will be distributing food from 9:30 until 10:30 am.

Those planning to attend should pre-register at www.EIFclient.com, although doing so does not guarantee a place in line.  There are some income guidelines.

The distribution is part of the Foodbank’s Foodmobile Program, a system of mobile food pantries designed to help bring nutritious food to rural or underserved areas.

The Clay County Ministerial Alliance food pantry is open every Monday from 9 to 11 am, at 1101 Austin Avenue in Flora.

title: WORLD’S LARGEST RESOLUTION
full_story:
State Representative Adam Niemerg passed House Resolution 684 to honor the life of James “Jim” Bolin of Casey who passed away in January.  Bolin was the visionary behind “Big Things in A Small Town” and collected 12 Guinness Book of World Records titles for 21 different objects, including the largest wind chime, largest rocking chair, and longest seesaw/teeter totter.

“Jim Bolin was known and loved by people everywhere, but most importantly by his family and friends in Casey,” said Rep. Niemerg.  “When the resolution states ‘a suitable copy be presented to his family,’ we thought, what could be more suitable than the world’s largest resolution?”

Rep. Niemerg and fellow resolution sponsors Rep. Brad Halbrook, Rep. Chris Miller, and Rep. Blaine Wilhour will present the resolution to Bolin’s family this afternoon at the Illinois State Capitol.  The House will convene at 12:00 noon.

title: FREE 38 SPECIAL CONCERT
full_story:
Fairgoers are in for a rockin’ good time at the 2026 Illinois State Fair as legendary southern rock band 38 Special takes the Grandstand stage for a FREE concert on Monday, August 17th.

For more than five decades, 38 Special has brought their signature blast of guitar-driven southern rock to audiences around the world.  Known for their infectious blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks, the band has produced a long list of hits that have stood the test of time, including “Hold On Loosely,” “Caught Up in You,” “Rockin’ Into the Night,” “If I’d Been the One,” and “Second Chance.”  With over 20 million albums sold, 38 Special continues to tour nationwide, delivering high-energy performances that showcase their timeless sound and unmistakable style.  Their music remains a staple on classic rock radio, and their live shows continue to draw fans of all generations.

“We’re always looking for ways to enhance the value of a day at the Fair,” said Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.  “Bringing in a band with the legacy and energy of 38 Special for a free show is a great way to make the Grandstand accessible and memorable for everyone.”

The FREE 38 Special concert takes place Monday, August 17th at the Illinois State Fair Grandstand.  Gates open at 7 pm and no ticket is required, but attendees must go through security screening prior to entering the Grandstand.

Mark your calendars for the 2026 Illinois State Fair, August 13th through August 23rd in Springfield.

Stay up to date with all the latest news and announcements from the Illinois State Fair by connecting with us via Facebook, Twitter and Instagram.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT IN STATE UP
full_story:
The Illinois unemployment rate in March was 5.1%, up from an even 5% in February and up from 4.6% in March 2025.

Total nonfarm payrolls increased over-the-month in March, up 8,400.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases include Private Education and Health Services, Professional and Business Services, and Government.  The industry sectors with the largest over-the-month job decreases included Trade, Transportation and Utilities, Financial Activities, and Manufacturing.

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were down 4,300.
